resources.string: Move text or small files between screens and cameras — no radio at all.

How it works
• The sender splits data into chunks and shows them as QR codes — two at a time. Each code carries: transfer ID, index, total and the CRC-32 of the whole content (format QT1:ID:INDEX:TOTAL:CRC32:DATA).
• Data is packed with Base45 so the QR uses alphanumeric mode (≈30 % more data per code than base64). Text is compressed (DEFLATE) when that helps.
• The receiver reads all codes in a camera frame, in any order, shows which chunks are missing, and verifies the CRC-32 when complete. Decoder (0.4.0): zxing-cpp (default, reads many and small codes per frame, with a 2× upscale retry for tiny codes) or the old Java ZXing (setting on the receive screen).
• Acknowledgment tones: each chunk i is answered with one of four tones chosen by i mod 4 — A0 1350, A1 1700, B0 2050, B1 2400 Hz — and 3050 Hz (long, quieter since 0.4.0) = all done. With "advance on tones" the sender listens with the microphone; both codes take their chunks from one shared queue (sender 0.5.0 / app 0.4.0), a code advances only when it hears the ack for exactly its chunk, and the two codes on screen always have different tones. A code that is not confirmed stays on screen (nothing is skipped); the PC page redraws such a code with another mask after a few seconds. Auto-advance (loop) is used only when you turn "advance on tones" off or press ⟳ — never automatically. "Test tones" on the receive screen lets you check that the sender (the PC page's mic diagnostics) hears all five tones.
• PC → phone: open web/sender.html (single offline file) in a desktop browser; it can listen with the PC microphone too.

No internet, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi or NFC is used. Keep the receiving phone ~20–40 cm from the screen so both codes are in view; lower the speed or chunk size if scanning is slow.

Auto-advance (loop) speed — not used in MIC / ACK mode
Advance on the receiver\'s tones (microphone, default). Off = auto-advance (loop)

Recommended. The receiver answers every chunk with a tone chosen by its index mod 4 (1350 / 1700 / 2050 / 2400 Hz). Both codes take their chunks from one shared queue: whichever code is confirmed first shows the next unconfirmed chunk, and the two codes on screen never share a tone. A code advances only when the sender hears the ack for exactly its chunk — no timeouts, stale or too-early acks are ignored, an unconfirmed code stays on screen — and the sender stops on the 3050 Hz done tone. It never switches to auto-advance by itself: without a microphone the codes wait and the ⟳ button offers the loop. Tip: on the receiver, \"test tones\" plays all five tones.
Microphone denied: the codes will not advance by themselves. Press ⟳ for auto-advance (loop).
